# Feed config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/feeds/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.FeedBlock` (ADR-083 D1) declaring a named, **transport-free** selection over the broker's topic space — the unit both ADR-083 egresses consume. The block label is the feed name.

A feed declares *what leaves*, never *how*: nothing here names a port, a protocol, a URL, or a credential. A transport **references** a feed; a feed never references a transport. That asymmetry is what lets a second egress (the D6 OTLP push exporter) share one selection model with the first (the D3 text-frame port) as an addition rather than a rewrite.

The boundary calls follow directly from it, and the test to apply is *does this state what leaves, or how it travels*. `max_rate_per_sec` lives **in** the feed, because a volume cap states how much of the stream is wanted — a selection concern. The D4 heartbeat interval does **not**, even though it looks like it wants to sit beside it: a heartbeat period is a property of the wire, and it is configured on the egress listener. Neither does the D12 `batch_window`, for the same reason and by the same argument: shedding reduces what you receive and batching reduces how often you are woken, so a delivery window is a wire property and lives on the listener too — which is what lets one feed be served to an agent consumer in batches and to a human tailing a terminal record-for-record, over the same selection, with neither having to be the other's compromise. The listener also carries `batch_max_records`, whose default is *derived* from this block's `max_rate_per_sec`.

`where` blocks are declarative predicates (`field` + `in`), not an expression language — ADR-083 Alt D defers CEL rather than refusing it, on the measured ground that CEL at workflow-linearization time and CEL per-record on a delivery path are different performance propositions. Multiple `where` blocks are ANDed; within one block `in` is a disjunction; the same `field` predicated twice is rejected rather than silently intersected.

A feed confers no reach. Per ADR-083 D2 the server expands `subscribe` into concrete topic filters and authorizes **each** expanded filter against the connecting principal's own grants, so a client sees the intersection of the feed and its own role — the feed answers *what does this consumer watch*, the role answers *what may it see*, and collapsing the two is how a curation edit silently becomes a privilege escalation. One authoring hazard worth restating (ADR-010:294): a feed spanning both the OTel and the events families needs **two** patterns, because the `<domain>` level in `_sys/v1/events/v1/<domain>/...` shifts every scope position one to the right and no single wildcard reaches both.

## Example

A minimal `feeds`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/feeds/example-feed.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

feed "example-feed" {
  subscribe = ["_sys/v1/events/v1/workorder/#"]
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | block label | Feed name — the identity an egress references. A feed confers no reach of its own (ADR-083 D2). |
| `description` | string | no | — | — | — | Human-readable description of what this feed watches and who consumes it. |
| `subscribe` | string[] | yes | — | — | — | MQTT-style topic filters this feed selects. Required and non-empty. A feed spanning both the OTel and events families needs two patterns — no single wildcard reaches both (ADR-083 D6). The {principal} token is refused rather than substituted: per-principal feed scoping is not available (ADR-083 D8). A filter naming the activity family _sys/v1/activity/v1/<partition>/... must name the partition level literally: a + there, or a # spanning it, claims reach across every partition and is refused at load (ADR-113 D4). A filter on the system-event family _sys/v1/events/v1/... must end in # or have the family's full level count; any other length matches no event and is refused at load (ADR-142 D6). Declare one feed per partition; a consumer narrows to a single Work Order at connect time (ADR-083 D5). |
| `where` | block (list) | no | — | — | — | Declarative predicates over decoded envelope fields. Multiple blocks are ANDed. Not an expression language (ADR-083 Alt D). |
| `max_rate_per_sec` | integer | no | — | — | — | Ceiling on records delivered per second. Unset or 0 means no cap; negative is rejected. |

## `where` block

Repeatable.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | string | yes | — | — | — | Decoded envelope field the predicate reads (e.g. "state"). |
| `in` | string[] | yes | — | — | — | Values that pass. Required and non-empty; a record whose field is not in this set is not delivered. |
